chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (AS), who said:
Verily, among the signs of fiqh (deep religious understanding) are forbearance and silence.

key_terms.الصَّمْتَ: samt — silence, deliberate restraint of speech; valued in Islamic tradition as protection from error and a mark of wisdom
key_terms.الْحِلْمَ: hilm — forbearance, gentleness, and measured self-restraint in the face of provocation; a core virtue of Islamic ethics
key_terms.الْفِقْهِ: fiqh — deep understanding of religion, encompassing both legal knowledge and spiritual insight; here contrasted with superficial learning

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of true fiqh (religious understanding) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam 'Ali al-Rida (AS) states that among the signs of fiqh — deep religious understanding — are forbearance (hilm) and silence (samt). These two virtues distinguish the truly learned from those who merely accumulate information.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan Al Neyshapouri, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the sings of the understanding (of the Religion), is the forbearance and the silence’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Muhammad ibn ‘Ism’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Of the signs of Fiqh, good understanding of religion is forbearance and quietness.”
